reason: At base, REGEX_FORMAT still matches Y{1,4}, and format() falls through unmatched 'Y'/'YYY' tokens to the timezone-offset fallback, so 'Y' returns an offset like '+0000' instead of the literal 'Y'.
At head, REGEX_FORMAT changed to YYYY|YY, so a lone 'Y' no longer matches and stays literal while 'YYY' resolves to '24Y', matching the expected output.
At base, #getDecodedParam already decodes params containing '%' via tryDecodeURIComponent, so %20 is returned as a space; the PR is a behavior-preserving refactor.
At head the refactor extracts tryDecodeURIComponent with identical decode-when-'%'-present semantics, so percent-encoded params still decode to the literal character.
At base, SortedEntry#reschedule never updates @score, so reading entry.score/entry.at after reschedule yields the stale pre-reschedule value, contradicting the test.
At head, reschedule sets @score = at.to_f after zincrby, so the in-memory handle immediately reflects the new time.
The change only touches parseRangesSpecifier (Range header) in ktor-http; Content-Type/charset parsing is a separate, unaffected code path that already works.
Same as base: the Range-header trimming change does not affect Content-Type charset parsing, which still reports 'text/plain' with charset 'UTF-8'.
The PR only changes download-failure logging in ComposerRepository; the zip archiving/timestamp logic is untouched, so archive timestamp preservation is unaffected and works.
The logging-only change is unrelated to archiving, so re-archiving still yields source-matching timestamps (no 1980 default).
The change is to CredentialCacheKey network prefix matching; System.Text.Json async deserialization of a nullable parent property is an unrelated, already-working feature.
CredentialCache change does not affect JSON (de)serialization, so sync and async paths both succeed equivalently.
The PR fixes FETCH FIRST on a WITH HOLD cursor; INET containment operators (<<= ANY) are unrelated SQL parsing/execution that already succeed.
The cursor FETCH FIRST fix is unrelated to INET >>= ANY parsing, which still parses and returns true.
At base, NO_PROXY entries are all prefixed as wildcard domains, so an IPv6 '::1' is transformed into an unparseable pattern causing an error on client construction.
At head, '::1' is recognized as an IPv6 hostname and mounted as all://[::1], so client construction succeeds without error.
At base, Series.str.match raised for any regex flag other than re.IGNORECASE, so enabling the dot-matches-newline (DOTALL) flag errors out instead of honoring it.
At head, DOTALL (and other non-IGNORECASE flags) are restored for both inline flags and compiled patterns, so 'a\nc' matches and 'ac' does not.
At base, freezing a chain with a group followed by more tasks mishandles recursive result parents, dropping child results of the parallel groups on reconstruction.
At head, prepare_steps updates prev_task/prev_res for groups in the middle of a chain, so all four child results are preserved.
The PR fixes the first-argument '--' case; a '--' appearing mid-arguments already terminated the first positional and handed '--check' to the trailing positional, so the test passed before and after.
The new terminator-handling branch also preserves correct mid-argument '--' handoff, so the first positional gets value1/value2 and the second gets --check.
At base, a late-arriving OSC11 response calls nvim_set_option_value('background',...) which triggers OptionSet (and ColorScheme), matching the test's expectation.
At head, the fix wraps the background set in :noautocmd, explicitly suppressing the OptionSet event, so the test's expectation that OptionSet fires is no longer met.
The change only reorders a compile-time @derive read for redacted-field Inspect deriving; required-field changeset validation behavior is unaffected and still flags the blank field.
The compile-time dependency reordering does not alter validation logic, so an omitted required field still yields an invalid changeset with a 'can't be blank' error.
